concerns.text: Task T001 is tagged `[P]` (parallel‑safe) but it produces `data/raw/checksums.json` which is a required input for T002. Running T001 in parallel with any task that reads `checksums.json` (e.g., T002) would create a race condition. The `[P]` tag is therefore inaccurate.

Task T002 is marked `[P]` yet it reads the checksum file generated by T001 and writes `data/processed/unified_fatigue.csv`, which is consumed by many downstream tasks (T003, T004, T008, T009, etc.). It cannot safely execute in parallel with its producer or any consumer; the `[P]` tag is invalid.
Task T003 is `[P]` but depends on the unified CSV from T002 and writes `runtime_summary.csv` that is later read by T011. Parallel execution with its producer/consumer would break the data flow.
Task T004 is `[P]` yet it consumes `unified_fatigue.csv` from T002 and produces feature‑set files used by T005. The tag misrepresents its ordering constraints.
Task T005 is `[P]` but reads feature‑set artifacts from T004 and writes model files consumed by T006, T007, T010, etc. It cannot be safely parallelised with those tasks.

Task T008 is `[P]` yet it reads the processed dataset produced by T002 and its result (`mediation_eligibility.json`) is required by T009. Parallel execution with its producer/consumer would cause ordering violations.
Task T009 is `[P]` but depends on the eligibility JSON from T008 and on the measured‑stress subset from T002. It must wait for those producers.
Task T010 is `[P]` yet it aggregates results from T003‑T009 and writes the final markdown report. It cannot run before all those producers have completed.
Task T011 is `[P]` but validates the runtime summary generated by T010 and the model training times from T005. It must be scheduled after those tasks.
Task T012 is `[P]` yet it lists artifact locations that are produced by earlier tasks (e.g., T010, T011). It should not be marked parallel‑safe.

Task T013 is `[P]` but modifies `spec.md`, a document that is referenced by many downstream tasks (e.g., T001‑T012) for traceability. Changing the spec while those tasks are running would break consistency; the tag should be removed or the task scheduled after all consumers.

Task T014 is `[P]` yet it also edits `spec.md` (the same file as T013). Concurrent execution with T013 or any task that reads the spec would cause nondeterministic behavior. The parallel‑safe tag is inappropriate.
